newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Peru rebels vow "political, not violent" response.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels vow "political, not violent" response.

text.p: Two members of the rebel group responsible for the hostage drama in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Peru promised that the group's response to their colleagues' deaths will be "political and not violent."

"Our response will not be through violence like those of (Peru's) President Alberto Fujimori," the two members of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) said, according to statements published on Tuesday by Bolivian private news agency Jatha.

The statements by Juan Carlos Caballero and Martin Serna Ponce, two confessed Peruvian MRTA members imprisoned in Bolivia, came after Peru's army last week ended the four-month stand-off by storming the ambassador's residence.
All 14 rebels were killed and all but one of the 72 hostages were rescued.
"With the death of our 14 comrades, state terrorism, the impunity of paramilitary groups and the policy of extermination have been institutionalized," said Caballero.
Caballero and Ponce are two of four Peruvian MRTA members imprisoned in Bolivia charged with the 1995 kidnapping of Bolivian businessman Samuel Doria Medina.

The 45-day kidnapping of Doria Medina led to the payment of a $1.2 million ransom. That money was used to finance the December attack on the Japanese residence in Lima, according to local press reports.
